seleccion.titulo: Vascularized brain organoids enable reconstruction of the human blood-brain barrier and neurovascular disease modelling
seleccion.resumen_previo: Se desarrolló una plataforma de organoides cerebrales humanos vascularizados que reconstruye características clave de la barrera hematoencefálica y su unidad neurovascular. El avance permite estudiar mecanismos específicamente humanos de formación de la barrera y modelos de enfermedad neurovascular, con potencial aplicación en xenotrasplantes a roedores inmunodeficientes.
seleccion.extracto: Abstract The human blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a dynamic neurovascular interface essential for brain development and homeostasis, yet human-specific mechanisms governing its formation and dysfunction remain difficult to study. Here we establish a scalable platform of vascularized human brain organoids that recapitulates key features of the neurovascular unit and BBB organisation. Early integration of endothelial and mural cells generates stable vascular networks with junctional architecture and BBB-associated transporter expression while preserving cortical development. seleccion.resumen_previo: Se identificó en Japón una cepa novedosa de rotavirus humano con un genoma quimérico que contiene segmentos de origen porcino, humano y felino. El hallazgo es relevante para entender los riesgos de zoonosis y recombinación viral en contextos donde circulan patógenos porcinos.
seleccion.extracto: Human G11P[25] rotaviruses reported to date have been porcine-like strains with relatively conserved Wa-like genomic backbones. seleccion.titulo: Multimodal precision diagnostics in clinical xenotransplantation
seleccion.resumen_previo: Se revisaron desafíos diagnósticos en xenotrasplantes: aunque se logró evitar el rechazo hiperagudo, surgen nuevas formas de lesión inmunológica que requieren detección temprana. El documento propone herramientas multimodales avanzadas para monitoreo de injertos.
seleccion.extracto: Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date.
